title: Etale cohomology in dimension zero
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $C$ be a separated finite-type
$k$-scheme of dimension at most zero, as allowed in
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. For an abelian etale sheaf
$F$, its etale cohomology is canonically

$$
 H^q(C,F)=
 \begin{cases}
  \displaystyle\prod_{c\in|C|}F_{\bar c},&q=0,\\
  0,&q>0,
 \end{cases}
$$

where the product is finite and $F_{\bar c}$ denotes the geometric stalk at
$c$.

proof.text: Apply AlgebraicGeometry.zero_dimensional_etale_finite, proved directly from Mathlib's locally Noetherian, locally Artinian and compact-discrete finiteness results. This gives the first conjunct.

Apply AlgebraicGeometry.zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology_rest to the same data, including the arbitrary geometric fields and the prescribed point equations. It supplies exactly the positive-degree subsingleton clause and invertibility of the canonical comparison/product-of-germs map. Pair this conjunction with finiteness by conjunction introduction.
